text.p: LME metals recovered in the afternoon as a wave of trade buying gave the market a shot in the arm, traders said.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index rose 1.36 points to 244.89.
On the LME, three months aluminium finished the afternoon kerb in the positive column at $1,584, up $2 on the day, after earlier touching a low of $1,565.
Copper also dipped, moving down to $2,572, before finding support and finishing the day at $2,582, a loss of $6.
Lead dropped to a 20-month low of $613 as more long liquidation battered prices before trade buying kicked in and sent them on a modest upswing to $622, up $1 on the day.
Nickel also hit stops, sliding as low as $7,100 before support buoyed the market. Last trade was $40 softer at $7,210.
Zinc edged up to a fresh peak at one point, adding $2 to Monday's high to hit $1,379, but scale-up selling and profit taking capped the move.
Tin dipped, but put on the brakes before reaching the recent low of $5,510, touching a low of $5,525.
Alloy closed weaker at $1,465, down from $1,475/80 on Monday.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mostly higher on gains in soybeans and on short covering tied to signals the market was oversold late Monday, traders said. CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed 1-1/2 cents higher to one cent lower, with July up one at $3.43-3/4.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly lower Tuesday, on moderate volumes, with the exception of silver. COMEX August gold ended down $1.10 at $343.70 an ounce, with the weak downtrend since early May still seen intact, though support has held three times around $343.00 an ounce, analysts noted. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $341.50/00, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $342.15 and the New York close Monday around $342.40/90.

NYMEX crude ended higher Tuesday ahead of tonight's weekly oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) which traders expected would report a healthy draw in crude inventories. "There was a lot of talk about API expectations. Some are looking for a five to six million barrel draw," said a New York crude trader. July crude ended 22 cents a barrel higher at $19.23. A consensus of trader estimates pegged the draw at 2.125 million barrels, with most estimates ranging between a draw of one and three million barrels.
